BOUNDARY: The empty-subspace case $A=\varnothing$ (ordinary homotopy) and the endpoint case $A=\{0,1\}$ (path homotopy) are both covered by the general argument. The set of maps with a prescribed restriction to $A$ may be empty; an equivalence relation on an empty set is trivially valid. No degenerate, coincident-map, or limiting case affects the logical structure—reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity hold for every continuous map without extra conditions.
